t: Number of Beautiful Pairs — First Digit vs Last Digit Coprimality
o: A pair (i<j) is beautiful iff firstDigit(nums[i]) and lastDigit(nums[j]) are coprime. With n ≤ 100 a direct O(n²) check is completely fine. A slightly smarter version precomputes gcd answers for digit pairs 1–9 and counts occurrences of each first/last digit, giving O(n + 81) work.
k: Only the first digit of the left element and last digit of the right element matter.

a.i: Extract digits and test every pair with math.gcd — tiny constraints make this optimal in practice.
s: For each i<j compute first digit of nums[i] and last digit of nums[j].

a.i: Precompute a 10×10 coprime table, tally first digits and last digits, then sum cntFirst[f] × cntLast[l] over coprime (f,l). Careful: for i=j exclusion, subtract pairs where the same element contributes both digits when gcd(first,last)==1.
s: Count first digits and last digits separately.
Answer = Σ coprime(f,l) · firstCnt[f] · lastCnt[l] − (elements whose own first/last digits are coprime).
a.t: O(n + 81) — linear pass plus constant table

w: Use brute force unless asked for better; the counting version matters if n were 10^5+. Pitfall in the counting approach: forgetting to subtract same-element pairs.
